{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''James Edward Pringle''' (born 20 January 1949) is a British [[astrophysicist]]. He is a [[professor]] of theoretical [[astronomy]] at the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge]] part of the [[University of Cambridge]].

His research is focused mainly on astrophysical [[fluid dynamics]] and [[accretion disc]]s, including, for example, the formation of [[star]]s and [[planet]]s, accretion of matter onto [[black hole]]s, and formation of [[astrophysical jet|jet]]s by accretion flows. In a 1984 paper, he and [[John Papaloizou]] showed that accretion disks in anisotropic stellar systems with constant specific angular momentum are unstable to non-axisymmetric global modes.<ref>{{cite journal | title = The dynamical stability of differentially rotating discs with constant specific angular momentum | bibcode = 1984MNRAS.208..721P | journal = Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. | author = Papaloizou, J. C. B. | author2 = Pringle, J. E. | volume = 208 | date = 1984 | issue = 4 | pages = 721&ndash;750|doi = 10.1093/mnras/208.4.721 | doi-access = free }}</ref> This phenomenon is now known as the [[Papaloizou–Pringle instability]].

He was awarded the [[Eddington Medal]] in 2009.<ref>{{Citation | title = RAS Awards and Prizes: RAS Awards 2009; Gold Medal: Prof. David Williams; Gold Medal: Prof. Eric Priest; Price Medal: Prof. Malcolm Sambridge; Eddington Medal: Prof. James Pringle | year = 2009 | journal = Astronomy and Geophysics | volume = 50 | issue = 1 | pages = a34| bibcode = 2009A&G....50a..34.| doi = 10.1111/j.1468-4004.2009.50134.x | doi-access = free }}</ref>
